'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Two separate [[roadside bombing]]s kill 13 civilians in [[Helmand Province|Helmand]] and [[Ghor Province|Ghor]] [[provinces of Afghanistan|Provinces]]. Meanwhile, militants stop a bus in western [[Afghanistan]], targeting [[Hazaras|Hazara]] passengers and killing three of them. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/official-roadside-bombings-afghanistan-kill-13-people-77801822 (ABC News)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Nigerian intelligence]] officials say that [[Boko Haram]] leader [[Abubakar Shekau]] has either been killed or critically injured after [[suicide bombing|detonating explosives]] in his house to avoid capture from the rival [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|IS–West African Province]] faction. Several other Boko Haram members are also killed in the attack. However, no secondary sources have confirmed Shekau's death. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/may/20/boko-haram-leader-abubakar-shekau-nigeria-forest (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**The [[United States]] sanctions two [[Houthi movement|Houthi]] leaders for their roles in the [[Marib campaign]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/20/us-imposes-sanctions-on-two-houthi-military-leaders (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**[[Israel]] and [[Hamas]] agree to a [[ceasefire]] in order to stop [[airstrike]]s in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] and the launching of rockets in Israel. The 11 days of conflict have killed 232 people in Gaza and 11 in Israel. [[Egypt]] agrees to observe the implementation of the ceasefire. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-middle-east-57183127 (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[ByteDance]] founder [[Zhang Yiming]], whose company owns [[TikTok]], announces that he will step down as [[CEO]] and that [[human resources]] chief Rubo Liang will succeed him. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/exclusive-bytedance-co-founder-zhang-yiming-step-down-ceo-2021-05-20/ (Reuters)]
*Following recommendations from the Council on Ethics, the [[Government Pension Fund of Norway]] drops two firms from its [[Portfolio (finance)|portfolio]] for doing business with [[Israeli settlements|illegal Israeli settlements]] in the occupied [[West Bank]]. The [[Norges Bank|Norges Bank Investment Management]] also blacklists a company for owning factories in [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/5/20/norway-wealth-fund-excludes-firms-linked-to-west-bank-settlemen (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[Argentine beef|Argentine cattle]] farmers begin a nine-day protest against the [[Government of Argentina|government]]'s implementation of a month-long restriction on meat exports to deter [[Economy of Argentina#Inflation|inflation]]. Farmers have agreed to suspend their sales of cattles to [[slaughterhouse]]s during the protest. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20210520-argentine-cattle-farmers-start-9-day-strike-against-export-pause (Radio France Internationale)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 wildfire season]]
**[[Wildfire]]s in [[Attica (region)|Attica]], [[Greece]], prompt the evacuation of several villages and monasteries as the fires spread throughout the [[Geraneia]] mountain range. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/greece-evacuates-villages-forest-fire-rages-corinth-region-2021-05-20/ (Reuters)]
*Thirteen people are killed and 29 injured after a bus overturned on a highway in [[Sukkar]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-59b188d6f5b404b1e2c408c225b53885 (AP News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Ontario]] [[Premier of Ontario|Premier]] [[Doug Ford]] unveils a three-step reopening plan as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases decline. [[Golf]], [[tennis]], [[basketball]], and other outdoor sports will be allowed to reopen on May 22, but the [[stay-at-home order]] will remain in place until June 2. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/ontario-reopening-plan-covid-19-third-wave-1.6033762 (CBC News)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iowa]]
*****[[Governor of Iowa|Iowa Governor]] [[Kim Reynolds]] signs a law prohibiting schools and businesses from imposing [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandates]]. She also signs a law that limits vaccine passports in [[Iowa|the state]]. [https://qctimes.com/news/local/education/updated-iowa-gov-reynolds-prohibits-k-12-schools-from-mandating-masks-effective-immediately/article_97f2c15b-0681-5886-ba6d-bd931c8402e4.amp.html (''Quad-City Times'')] [https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2021/05/20/iowa-gov-kim-reynolds-vaccine-passports-law-limiting-use-prove-covid-vaccination/5074442001/ (''The Des Moines Register'')]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****The [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]] announces its approval for measures allowing the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] to be stored at regular [[refrigerator]] temperatures for up to 30 days before administration. Previously, the agency had only allowed such storage for five days. [https://time.com/6049966/pfizer-biontech-vacccine-refrigeration-storage-time/ (''Time'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nicaragua]]
****[[Nicaragua]] approves the emergency use of the single-dose [[Sputnik Light]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.pharmiweb.com/press-release/2021-05-20/single-dose-sputnik-light-vaccine-approved-for-use-in-nicaragua (PharmiWeb)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Panama]]
****[[Panama]] closes its border with [[Colombia]] due to COVID-19 concerns. The [[Government of Colombia|Colombian government]] had recently reopened the border, which had been closed since March 2020. Panama has so far recorded more than 370,000 COVID-19 cases and 6,300 deaths. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/panama-says-will-temporarily-close-border-with-colombia-over-covid-19-risk-2021-05-20/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] suspends a reciprocal green lane arrangement with [[Singapore]] until further notice following the worsening situation of the pandemic in the latter country. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/brunei-suspends-reciprocal-green-lane-singapore-14849522 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
****[[Laos]] extends its nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for another 15 days until June 4 as the number of COVID-19 cases continues to increase. [https://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/269559543/laos-extends-lockdown-as-covid-19-cases-continue-to-surge (Big News Network)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 6,806 new cases of [[COVID-19]], thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 492,302. The country also reports a record 59 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,099. [https://www.malaymail.com/amp/news/malaysia/2021/05/20/malaysias-new-covid-19-infections-leap-to-6806-beating-previous-days-record/1975654 (''Malay Mail'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
****President [[Alberto Fernández]] announces a nine-day nationwide lockdown to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/argentina-tighten-lockdown-pandemic-rages-sources-say-2021-05-20/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Brazil]] reports its first cases of the Lineage B.1.617 variant, which was first discovered in [[India]]. The variant had been detected among a group of six crew members of a ship travelling from [[South Africa]] to deliver [[iron ore]] in [[São Luís, Maranhão]]. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/351090-brazil-confirms-first-cases-of-indian-covid-variant (Geo News)] [https://english.alarabiya.net/amp/coronavirus/2021/05/20/Brazil-confirms-first-cases-of-Indian-COVID-19-variant?fbclid=IwAR39hCrohruQrE9RBVRpoCrvv-cGjPs9XqNwmubOmt26ImYYW7gz1wWdPP8 (Al Arabiya English)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
***[[Prince William, Duke of Cambridge]], receives his first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/prince-william-duke-of-cambridge-first-dose-covid-19-vaccine/#app (CBS News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-57185584 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[European Commission]] signs a third contract with [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]] to secure 1.8 billion doses of its [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-eu-secures-18-billion-doses-of-biontech-pfizer-covid-vaccine/a-57596104 (Deutsche Welle)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on international relations]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
**The [[International Institute for Strategic Studies]] cancels the [[Shangri-La Dialogue]] intergovernmental forum which would have been held in [[Singapore]] on June 4–5 due to the worsening of the COVID-19 pandemic situation in the country. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210520-singapore-security-forum-cancelled-due-to-covid (France 24)]
*[[China–Lithuania relations]]
**Three-fifths of the [[Seimas|Lithuanian Parliament]] vote to pass a nonbinding resolution condemning the [[Xinjiang internment camps|forced internment]] of Muslim [[Uyghurs]] as [[Uyghur genocide|genocide]], demanding the repeal of the [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]], and calling for international observers to be allowed to enter [[Tibet]] and for the Chinese government to begin negotiations with the [[14th Dalai Lama|current Dalai Lama]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/lithuanian-parliament-latest-call-chinas-treatment-uyghurs-genocide-2021-05-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Ethiopia]] announces that it will proceed with plans to start generating power from the controversial [[Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam]] in the coming [[rainy season]] between June and August. The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ethiopia)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] also says that it will not tolerate "any move that's aimed at disrupting the water filling process, its operation and water releasing scheme". [https://apnews.com/article/ethiopia-africa-middle-east-business-e3ac3440da1ebb71c1d239132647086c (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Colonial Pipeline cyberattack]]
**In the aftermath of the attack, it is revealed at a [[United States Senate Committee on Armed Services|Senate Armed Services cyber subcommittee]] hearing that the [[United States Department of Homeland Security|Department of Homeland Security]] was not alerted to the ransomware attack and that the [[United States Department of Justice|Justice Department]] was not alerted to the ransom type or the amount of money demanded, prompting discussion about the numerous information silos in the government and difficulties of information-sharing between them. [https://news.usni.org/2021/05/18/lawmakers-grill-pentagon-homeland-security-officials-on-how-to-prevent-another-colonial-pipeline-style-attack (USNI News)]
**Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic publishes a [[bitcoin]] wallet report showing that $90 million in bitcoin ransom payments were made to [[DarkSide (hacking group)|DarkSide]] or DarkSide affiliates over the last year, originating from 47 distinct wallets. According to a DarkTracer release of 2,226 victim organizations since May 2019, 99 organizations have been infected with the DarkSide malware – suggesting that approximately 47% of victims paid a ransom, and that the average payment was $1.9 million. The DarkSide developer has received bitcoins worth $15.5 million (17%), with the remaining $74.7 million (83%) going to the various affiliates. [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/colonial-pipeline-hackers-received-$90-million-ransom-victim?fbclid=IwAR2h6ec41MuchXPLefKvz4uL4jMZE8cvwt1TOZCL47LffdWg--Ghp9s6hWo (''The Washington Examiner'')] [https://www.foxbusiness.com/money/colonial-pipeline-hacker-darkside-reaped-90m-from-victims (Fox Business)]
*[[International protests over the 2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**In [[Midtown Manhattan|Midtown]] [[Manhattan]], pro-[[Palestinians|Palestinian]] and pro-[[Israel]] protesters clash at [[Times Square]] despite a ceasefire being announced between Israel and [[Hamas]] militants. One protester suffers a minor burn after fireworks were thrown from a car. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/times-square-brawl-pro-israel-and-pro-palestinian-protesters-clash (Fox News)] [https://www.newsweek.com/pro-palestine-pro-israel-protesters-clash-cease-fire-announced-1593526 (''Newsweek'')]
*[[Xenophobia and racism related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] signs the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act, a bill that would expedite anti-Asian hate crime reviews to the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/20/us/politics/biden-asian-hate-crimes-bill.html (''The New York Times'')]
*A fight between rival gangs erupts in a jail in [[Quetzaltenango]], [[Guatemala]], resulting in the deaths of seven people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-57181767 (BBC News)]
*The [[Constitutional Council (France)|French Constitutional Council]] strikes down Article 24 of the so-called [[Global security law proposal|global security law]], which criminalized the sharing of images that could reveal the identity of [[Law enforcement in France|police officers]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/05/20/france-s-constitutional-council-rejects-controversial-move-to-restrict-images-of-police (Euronews)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Ethiopian general election]]
**After delaying it twice, the [[National Election Board of Ethiopia]] schedules elections for June 21. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopia-hold-delayed-elections-june-21-vote-board-2021-05-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[International reactions to the 2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Bernie Sanders]] of [[Vermont]] introduces a resolution that would block an arms sale of [[United States dollar|$]]735 million in weapons to [[Israel]] in response to the conflict between [[Israel]] and [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/israel-gaza-us-weapons-sale-bernie-sanders-resolution/ (CBS News)]
*The [[Central Electoral Commission of Kyrgyzstan]] announces that it has invalidated the results of the [[Bishkek]] City Council elections. During a meeting, Chairwoman Nurzhan Shaildabekova called for free elections. [https://m.akipress.com/news:658406:Central_Election_Commission_cancels_Bishkek_local_council_election_results/?fbclid=IwAR3s_ksPwZwSEqZj7nc-QJmO-jjne1a_yIsP-xOhD0pNKU_Xi0AO925M59s (AKIpress News Agency)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Microsoft]] announces that it will discontinue support for [[Internet Explorer]] on June 15, 2022. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/microsoft-unplug-internet-explorer-it-seeks-edge-browser-war-2021-05-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Copa América]], [[2021 Colombian protests]]
**The [[CONMEBOL]], South America's football governing body, announces that [[Colombia]] will no longer co-host the [[2021 Copa América]] with Argentina as the country is currently experiencing [[2021 Colombian protests|social unrest]]. [https://apnews.com/article/colombia-copa-america-health-coronavirus-pandemic-soccer-02b9ddd1e0a16f0d68e7638226862546?fbclid=IwAR0U5sMWawwFkk4fqLjU9hyFBT0ufPc96D3B0GthvMq6F84kqAKSpRXRBsQ (Associated Press)]
